answer: A proposed marble exchange admits each earning key per round only when independent receivers confirm a unique 10 Mbps signal during a shared 60-second test; failures lose earning access, so every extra alias needs another 10 Mbps of upload capacity. The karst relay network tests all keys concurrently with distinct, key-bound random streams: one transmission cannot count for multiple keys. Receivers must be independent and payloads incompressible; collusion and rented high-capacity links remain weaknesses.
